# Buyer Quirk Sheet: eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality

- **Buyer:** eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality (incl. eThekwini Transport Authority as an internal client department)
- **Kind:** Metro (Category A municipality, KwaZulu-Natal)
- **Packs sampled:** 10 total — 1 structured analysis pack + 9 raw tender documents
  - `ethekwini-hygiene-services` (analysis JSON; tender 35007-1T, hygiene/cleaning of public transport ablutions, Eastern Region)
  - `ocds-9t57fa-165894` — 36487-1R, Upgrade of Zezwe/Mvoti/Ntaka/Landa Road, Ntuzuma (roads/stormwater, civil works)
  - `ocds-9t57fa-164278` — 35901-1M, Rates-based road & stormwater maintenance, North Central Region (36 months)
  - `ocds-9t57fa-164257` — 36514-5E, AMI electricity meter installation (36 months)
  - `ocds-9t57fa-165911` — 36720-1T, Supply & install public transport shelters, Southern Region
  - `ocds-9t57fa-165908` — Supply & install public transport shelters, Western Region (companion contract to 36720-1T)
  - `ocds-9t57fa-164268` — 36343-1J, Panel for panel-beating services, light motor/commercial vehicles (36 months)
  - `ocds-9t57fa-164262` — 36561-5E, Supply of goods (goods/local-content-weighted contract)
  - `ocds-9t57fa-164367` — 34963-1T, Hygiene services of public transport ablutions, Northern Region (sibling to the 35007-1T hygiene pack)
  - `ocds-9t57fa-164641` — 1F-36870, Cash-in-transit services (12 months)
- **Date:** 2026-08

---

## Submission channel & rules

eThekwini runs a **mandatory dual-channel submission** on every sampled pack: a physical hard-copy tender placed in the Tender Box, **plus** a parallel electronic submission through the Municipality's own JDE system (Supplier Self-Service / "ESP Module"), not a generic eTenders portal upload. The hard copy is explicitly the legally controlling version.

- "The Tender Offer (hard copy) shall be delivered to: The Tender Box in the foyer of the Municipal Building,166 KE Masinga Road, Durban... An electronic submission, via the eThekwini Municipality JDE System (ESP Module), is also to be made... Notwithstanding the electronic submission, a tender offer will only be deemed valid if the 'hard copy' submission has been made." (ocds-9t57fa-165894, also verbatim in ocds-9t57fa-164278)
- The hygiene pack states the identical-copy rule even more sharply: "Notwithstanding the electronic submission, a tender offer will only be deemed valid if the 'hard copy' submission has been made... if the electronic copy is found not to be identical to the hard copy, the Tender Offer shall be deemed invalid." (ethekwini-hygiene-services) — this identical-copy requirement was not found verbatim in the sampled infrastructure packs, so treat it as pack/contract-specific rather than universal until confirmed elsewhere.
- Facsimile and e-mail are explicitly rejected as channels: "Accept that tender offers submitted by facsimile or e-mail will be rejected by the employer, unless stated otherwise in the Tender Data." (ocds-9t57fa-165894). The hygiene pack reiterates: "Facsimile, email, and posted tenders are explicitly not accepted."
- Sealing/labeling: "Seal the original and each copy of the tender offer as separate packages marking the packages as 'ORIGINAL' and 'COPY'... state on the outside the employer's address and identification details... as well as the tenderer's name and contact address," then seal both inside one further outer package. (ocds-9t57fa-165894). The hygiene pack's plain-language version: "Sealed tender addressed to the City Manager and clearly marked with the tender number." Goods tender ocds-9t57fa-164262 confirms the same convention: "Sealed Tenders, addressed to the City Manager and marked with the Tender Number, are to be placed in [the Tender Box]."
- Bidders bear the delivery risk: "proof of posting shall not be accepted as proof of delivery" and late tenders are simply returned unopened. Attendance/access issues with the JDE/ESP system are explicitly the bidder's own responsibility to resolve before the deadline (ethekwini-hygiene-services).

## Municipal-arrears / rates clause

No fixed day-count grace window (e.g. "90 days") was observed — eThekwini's clause is closer to zero-tolerance at the point of award, with an escape valve only via a formal Acknowledgement of Debt (AOD) already in place by the closing date. It applies to the tenderer's obligations to **any** municipality, not just eThekwini itself.

- "Tenderers are to refer to Returnable Form: Declaration of Municipal Fees to certify that they have no undisputed commitments for municipal services towards any municipality. Prior to an award, a Tenderer's municipal rates and taxes cannot be in arrears. Should a Tenderer be in arrears with respect to municipal services and has formalised an agreement with the respective municipality to offset the arrears, the agreement must be in place at time of tender closing." (ocds-9t57fa-165894, repeated verbatim in ocds-9t57fa-164278, ocds-9t57fa-164257, ocds-9t57fa-165911, ocds-9t57fa-165908)
- Consistent with the "Declaration of Municipal Fees" returnable form on the goods/services packs: "Only those Bidders whose municipal fees are fully paid, or those that have concluded acknowledgement of debt agreements with the Municipality, are eligible to tender." (ocds-9t57fa-164268, ocds-9t57fa-164262, ocds-9t57fa-164367, ocds-9t57fa-164641; also ethekwini-hygiene-services)
- It applies even to bidders whose home municipality is not eThekwini — the hygiene pack requires attaching the *other* municipality's account/agreement: "applies even to tenderers outside eThekwini (must attach other municipality's account/agreement)." (ethekwini-hygiene-services)
- Failure to state account numbers or sign the declaration is itself fatal, independent of actual arrears status: "Failure to include account numbers or sign will invalidate the tender." (ethekwini-hygiene-services)

## B-BBEE treatment

Preference points only (no hard pre-qualification B-BBEE gate observed) — but the points are structurally heavy and the "specific goal" basket **varies by contract type**, which is itself a quirk worth flagging.

- Standard system is the 80/20 PPPFA points system (90/10 above R50m on at least one pack): "The 80/20 preference points system, for requirements with a Rand value of up to R50,000,000 (all applicable taxes included), will be applied." (ocds-9t57fa-165911)
- Unusually, on at least one pack the operative system (80/20 vs 90/10) is **not yet fixed at advertising** and depends on the lowest acceptable bid price received: "It is unclear (at the time of advertising) which of the two preference point systems applies, either the 80/20 or 90/10 preference point system will apply, determined by the price offered by the lowest acceptable tender." (ocds-9t57fa-164278, also ocds-9t57fa-165911) — bidders cannot know their maximum achievable preference points until bid opening.
- On construction/services packs the specific-goal basket is Ownership (Race: Black) + RDP/locality, weighted 75%/25% within the 20 preference points: "Ownership Goal: Race (Black)... 75%... max 15 of 20 points" and "RDP Goal: promotion of South African owned enterprises... 25%... max 5 of 20 points" with locality scaled ETM(5) > KZN(3.5) > South Africa(2) > outside SA(0) (ethekwini-hygiene-services; matching structure and locality scale also appears in ocds-9t57fa-164257 with a 50%/50% ownership/locality split and a Race scale capped at 2 points).
- On the sampled goods/supply tender the goal basket is entirely different — Gender (not Race) ownership at 30%, Locality at 30%, and "Local content and production"/business-type (retailer/wholesaler/distributor/manufacturer) at 40%: "RDP GOAL: OWNERSHIP GOAL... GOAL WEIGHTING: 30%... Gender: Female (100%)" and "GOAL WEIGHTING: 40%... Local content and production... Manufacturer 20" (ocds-9t57fa-164262). Locality scale here goes further, rewarding ETM specifically at the top: "Not in South Africa 0 / South Africa 5 / KZN 10 / ETM 20."
- Evidence required is standardised across packs: CIPC registration, CSD report, B-BBEE Certificate (or Consolidated Certificate for JV/Consortium/Trust), and the underlying JV/Consortium/Trust agreement — "Failure to provide any 'proof of claim' documentation will result in zero (0) points being awarded." (ocds-9t57fa-164262; consistent wording in ethekwini-hygiene-services)
- Mandatory post-award subcontracting-to-Black-owned-enterprise goals recur across contract types with an identical penalty formula (0.5% of contract value per 1% of shortfall), though the percentage goal itself varies by contract: 30% subcontracting goal in the hygiene pack (ethekwini-hygiene-services) versus 10% in the road-upgrade civil works pack — "the contractor must allow for a minimum of 10% of the contract value... to be subcontracted to contractors who are >51% owned by Black People... The penalty for not achieving the specified Sub-Contracting Goal will be 0.5% of the contract value... for every 1% not achieved." (ocds-9t57fa-165894)

## Cure/condonation policy

eThekwini operates a visible two/three-tier severity ladder rather than treating every defect as automatically fatal, though the great majority of returnable-document failures are drafted as hard, automatic invalidation with no cure path.

- **Hard/fatal, no cure** — most core returnables: "Failure of a Tenderer to complete, in its entirety, and sign the Official Tender Form will invalidate the tender." / "Failure to include account numbers or sign will invalidate the tender." / "Failure to include the required document will make the tender submission non-responsive." (ethekwini-hygiene-services)
- **Discretionary/softer tier** for at least one declaration: the OHS Act declaration is drafted as prejudicing rather than automatically killing the bid — "failure to complete and execute this declaration to the satisfaction of the Client will mean that this company is unable to comply... and accept that this tender will be prejudiced and may be rejected at the discretion of the Client." (ocds-9t57fa-165894) — a materially softer standard ("may be rejected", buyer discretion) than the "will invalidate" language used elsewhere.
- **Genuine, bounded cure mechanism** exists for arithmetic/pricing errors and general fine-tuning, but explicitly may not change competitive standing: "the employer may request that tenders be clarified, specified and fine-tuned in order to improve a tenderer's competitive position provided that such clarification, specification, fine-tuning or additional information does not alter any fundamental aspects of the offers" (ocds-9t57fa-165894) and "Reject a tender offer if the Tenderer does not accept the correction of the arithmetical error in the manner described in C.3.9.4." (ocds-9t57fa-164257) — so a bidder can be asked to accept a correction, but refusing the buyer's correction is itself a rejection ground.
- Requests for clarification during evaluation carry their own hard deadline with no observed grace: "The Tenderer must supply the requested information within the time specified. Failure to comply will render the tender non-responsive." (ethekwini-hygiene-services)
- No general post-submission "cure window" for missing mandatory returnables (e.g. no SBD-style "please resubmit within X days") was observed in the sampled packs — condonation appears limited to the arithmetic-correction and OHS-declaration cases above. Treat broader condonation practice as **not observed in sampled packs**.

## Security/vetting requirements

- **Not observed in sampled packs**: no post-award personnel vetting, integrity pact, security-clearance, or POPIA consent/data-protection clause was found in any of the 10 packs (explicit keyword searches for "POPIA", "vetting", "security clearance", "integrity pact", "background check" returned no matches).
- What does exist is sector-specific regulatory licensing rather than buyer-side vetting: the cash-in-transit pack requires PSIRA (private security industry) registration for the company and its directors, and the service is explicitly described as armed: "Authority (PSIRA) for the Company and Directors of the company" and "the service hereby called for is required for armed security to collect sealed containers" (ocds-9t57fa-164641). This is licensing-as-eligibility, not a municipal vetting/integrity process, so it is noted separately rather than folded into "vetting."
- The closest thing to an integrity control is the standard SCM anti-corruption apparatus common to all South African organs of state — MBD 9 (Certificate of Independent Bid Determination against collusion) and MBD 8 (past-SCM-practices declaration covering fraud/corruption convictions and restricted-supplier status) — both present as returnables (ethekwini-hygiene-services), but these are National Treasury standard forms, not an eThekwini-specific vetting regime.

## Financial demands

- **Performance guarantee** is a scaled table tied to contract value rather than a flat percentage: "Value of Contract (incl. VAT): Less than or equal to R1m = Nil; Greater than R1m and up to R10m = 5% of the Contract Sum; Greater than R10m = 10% of the Contract Sum." (ocds-9t57fa-165894)
- **Retention**: 10% retention on amounts due, capped at a limit of 5% of the Contract Sum/Price, with no interest paid on retention held: "The percentage retention on the amounts due to the Contractor is 10%. The limit of 'retention money' is 5% of the Contract Sum... Interest will not be paid on retention withheld by the Employer." (ocds-9t57fa-165894)
- **Insurance**: on the sampled civil-works pack, liability insurance is fixed at "The limit of indemnity for liability insurance: R10,000,000," plus a SASRIA Special Risks coupon policy issued jointly in the names of Council and Contractor for the full value of the works (ocds-9t57fa-165894). General conditions caution bidders to obtain their own advice since employer-provided cover may not be comprehensive: "the extent of insurance to be provided by the employer (if any) might not be for the full cover required... The tenderer is advised to seek qualified advice regarding insurance." (ocds-9t57fa-165894)
- **Audited financial statements** are gated by contract value, not universal: "For all procurement expected to exceed R10 million (all applicable taxes included), bidders must complete [MBD 5]... audited annual financial statements for past 3 years." (ocds-9t57fa-164268; consistent trigger threshold in ethekwini-hygiene-services)
- **CIDB grading** is a hard eligibility gate on construction-class work, calculated against tender value, including for JV lead partners and combined JV gradings: "Only those Tenderers who are registered ('Active') with the CIDB (at time of tender closing), in a contractor grading designation equal to or higher than a contractor grading designation determined in accordance with the sum tendered... Tenderers found to be inactive, suspended, or not meeting the required grading shall be deemed non-responsive." (ocds-9t57fa-165894)
- **Bank letters/credit ratings**: **Not observed in sampled packs** — no bank confidential reference letter or credit-rating requirement was found in any of the 10 packs.
- **Objection/appeal fee** is a distinctive standing financial demand on the process itself, not the bid: a non-refundable R6,131 (incl. VAT) administration fee must be paid before any post-award objection is even processed, confirmed identically in two independent packs: "Any objection will only be processed upon receipt of a non-refundable administration fee of R6,131.00 (including VAT), as stipulated in the Municipality's current SCM Policy." (ocds-9t57fa-165894, verbatim also in ocds-9t57fa-164268 and referenced in ethekwini-hygiene-services).

## Functionality norms

Functionality practice is inconsistent across contract types — sometimes a scored gate with a stated minimum, sometimes an unweighted pass/fail compliance check, and on at least one large civil-works pack not used at all.

- **Not used at all** on the road-upgrade civil works pack: "FUNCTIONALITY will not be used in the evaluation of tenders." (ocds-9t57fa-165894)
- **Scored with an explicit minimum threshold** on the AMI metering services pack: "FUNCTIONALITY will be used in the evaluation of tenders... The minimum score for FUNCTIONALITY is 70 points. Those tenders not achieving the minimum score will be deemed non-responsive." (ocds-9t57fa-164257)
- **Unweighted pass/fail gate**, not a scored functionality criterion, on the hygiene pack — experience and COID compliance are pre-conditions checked before price/preference scoring rather than points-weighted: "Experience of the bidder (1 PROJECT WITH A MINIMUM OF 12 MONTHS) in cleaning of public ablutions (proof in the form of Letters of Award, Reference Letters must be submitted)" is listed as a compliance gate with no numeric weight (ethekwini-hygiene-services).
- Where functionality does apply, the actual criteria/weights/minimum score live in the contract-specific "SCT" (Special Conditions of Tender) rather than the boilerplate T1 document: "Evaluation points for price and preference will only be calculated for Bidders who comply with the contractual and technical specification, and if applicable, have attained the minimum Functionality Score as stated in the SCT." (ocds-9t57fa-164268, ocds-9t57fa-164262, ocds-9t57fa-164367, ocds-9t57fa-164641) — bidders must check the specific SCT/Tender Data for each tender rather than assuming a metro-wide functionality threshold.

## Distinctive kill rules / quirks

- **Dual-channel submission with hard-copy supremacy**: a valid electronic JDE/ESP submission alone is never sufficient; the physical hard copy is what makes the tender valid, and at least one pack goes further, deeming the whole tender invalid if the two copies are not identical (ethekwini-hygiene-services; ocds-9t57fa-165894).
- **Preference system chosen retroactively by price**: on at least two packs, whether 80/20 or 90/10 applies is not fixed until the lowest acceptable bid is known — bidders cannot compute their own maximum achievable preference points in advance (ocds-9t57fa-164278, ocds-9t57fa-165911).
- **Multi-contract bundling with single-award cap**: eThekwini frequently advertises several near-identical regional contracts simultaneously and caps a bidder to one award even if they are the most responsive bidder on more than one, resolved via a "comparative value matrix" for best overall value — observed in both the hygiene-services family (four contracts: 34963-1T/35005-1T/35006-1T/35007-1T) and the transport-shelter family (36720-1T Southern + companion Western contract): "Contracts 1T-36720 and 1T-36501 are of the same nature and will be evaluated and awarded simultaneously. Most responsive bidders will be limited to one award for the above contracts." (ocds-9t57fa-165911; matching language in ethekwini-hygiene-services)
- **Mandatory local presence for the contract duration**: "The service provider must have, for the duration of the contract, a local presence (within the geographical eThekwini boundary)." (ethekwini-hygiene-services) — this is a performance/eligibility condition layered on top of, and distinct from, the CSD-address-based locality preference points.
- **Attendance at compulsory clarification meetings is a hard, name-matched gate**: only entities whose representative personally signs the attendance register in the tendering entity's own name are evaluated at all, regardless of document completeness — "Tenders will only be evaluated from those tendering entities appearing on the attendance list." (ethekwini-hygiene-services)
- **No CPI/price escalation during fixed multi-year term** on at least the hygiene pack: prices must be held firm for the full 24-month term with no statutory-increase pass-through, shifting all inflation risk to the bidder at tender stage (ethekwini-hygiene-services) — contrasts with the civil-works pack, which does carry a formal Contract Price Adjustment Factor with published labour/material/fuel/plant indices (ocds-9t57fa-165894).
- **Granular, itemised operational penalty regimes**: rather than a single generic breach-of-contract clause, penalties are itemised per incident/per day at specific Rand values (e.g. R2,000/day for late completion of civil works; R100–R500 per facility/day/incident on the hygiene contract) — signalling the buyer audits performance closely at an operational level, not just at milestone/final-acceptance stage (ocds-9t57fa-165894; ethekwini-hygiene-services).
- **Standing, non-refundable objection fee (R6,131 incl. VAT)** that must be paid before any unsuccessful bidder's appeal against an award decision is even processed — a distinctive, buyer-specific financial gate on the remedy process itself, confirmed identically across two independent packs (ocds-9t57fa-165894, ocds-9t57fa-164268).
